repo.description: Git URL of the upstream harness.

binary.description: Name of the executable the harness installs, e.g. opencode.

installer.description: The harness's official installer. When a user installs a mod for a harness they do not have, the CLI shows this command and runs it if they say yes.

command.description: Shell command from the harness's own install docs, e.g. curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install | bash.

paths.description: Folders the installer puts the binary in (~ is the home folder), so it is found before a new shell picks up the PATH line the installer added.

requirements.description: What a build needs on the machine, checked before anything is fetched or built. Each is a command that must be on PATH, or a check, a shell command that must succeed (for a library, say), on every OS or only on os. What is missing is installed with one line: every package in one install with the package manager found, then the install commands.

os.description: Only on this OS, as Node names it.

hint.description: What to install, shown when it is missing.

name.description: What it is, for the summary: "a C compiler".

packages.description: Its package for each package manager; every missing one goes into one install line.

install.description: A command that installs it, when it is not a package (rustup, say).
Shell command run in the checkout root before building.

buildInstall.description: Optional. The dependency install a build needs, when it is less than `install` (e.g. only the packages the build uses). Builds run it; a typecheck and `openmods dev` run `install`.

build.description: Shell command run in the checkout root that produces the artifact.

artifact.description: Path of the built executable relative to the checkout root. {os} and {arch} are substituted with Node's process.platform and process.arch.

keep.description: The folder, relative to the harness checkout, that holds the binary and everything it needs beside it, such as helper executables and resources. It is copied whole for each build, and artifact must be inside it. When unset, only the binary is kept.

dev.description: Shell command that runs a clone of the harness from source, for `openmods dev`. {root} is the clone's path and {version} a version like 1.18.32+my-mod-dev; the user's arguments are appended. It runs in the user's project folder with the release's pinned toolchain on PATH, and should end in exec.

env.description: Environment variables the modded build runs with, and a clone under `openmods dev`. For settings a modded build needs, such as turning off the harness's own self-update, since OpenMods offers the updates.

args.description: Arguments the modded build, and a clone under `openmods dev`, always start with, before the user's. For a setting a modded build needs next to the stock one that has no environment variable, such as turning off Codex's update check, since OpenMods offers the updates. They are the harness's own switches: OpenMods never changes a harness's code.

stockWhen.description: Arguments that start the user's stock harness instead of the modded build: a word without a leading - as the command (see valueOptions), an option anywhere; a trailing * matches its start; after -- nothing counts. For uses that share state with the stock harness, such as Codex's agents overview and --remote, which set up Codex's shared background server: from the modded build, stock Codex would then run modded code. With no stock harness to be found, the run stops and says so.

valueOptions.description: The harness's options that take a value as the next argument, such as -m for a model. With them the launcher finds the command word (the first argument that is neither an option nor such a value), which stockWhen and argsUnless words without a leading - are matched against, so a prompt that happens to be one of those words is not taken for the command.

sharedServer.description: A server the stock harness keeps in the user's home and shares between its runs, such as Codex's background server. `binary` is its program, relative to `home` (or the folder `homeEnv` names), and `versionFile` a JSON file beside it with the version it was packaged with, read and never run; `reset` is the stock harness's own command that puts it back to the stock program. When that server is a copy of a modded build (left by an older openmods), status and update say so and give the command; OpenMods itself never changes it.

sameRelease.description: What the launcher does when the user's stock harness is the very release the modded build is made from, such as OpenCode sharing session history with it. `stockVersion` is an extended regular expression whose first group is the release, found in the stock harness's program (read, never run; kept until that program changes). Then: `stockWhen` arguments (matched as in stockWhen) start the stock harness, for uses of a background service it shares; `env` is set, unless the mods change a file matching one of `envUnlessModsChange` (globs of the harness's files), such as its database tables; and `argsLast.args` go after the user's arguments (before a --), unless they include one of `argsLast.unless`. All of it is the harness's own switches: OpenMods never changes a harness's code.

argsUnless.description: More arguments to start with, after `args`, unless the user's arguments include one of `given` (a word as typed; a trailing * matches its start). For a switch the harness refuses in some uses, such as Codex's --no-daemon, which `codex agents` and --remote reject.

releaseTagPattern.description: Glob for release tags, used by the compatibility checker.

latestRelease.description: Where the harness's own release channel says which release is newest, for a harness that does not publish its releases on GitHub. The URL answers JSON with a "version"; the release watch builds the tag from it. Without this, the newest GitHub release is used.

url.description: URL answering JSON with a "version" field.

tag.description: The release tag, with {version} in place of the version, e.g. v{version}.

typecheck.description: Shell command run in the checkout root that type-checks the harness without producing a binary, e.g. cargo check or tsc. The release watch uses it to verify mods against a new release; the full build runs once per harness release and on a mod's pull request.

recipe.description: What our install, typecheck and build commands depend on in the harness's repo. When a new release changes any of it, the release watch holds the harness's mods until a person runs the harness build workflow. Each entry watches a whole file, or only its lines matching `lines` (a regex).
